_comment_mutate: src/lib takes .tsx as well as .ts. The four React context files there were never deliberately excluded; the .ts-only glob simply never reached them, leaving ThemeContext.tsx unmeasured despite its 319-line test file. constants-generated.ts is machine-written from api/pkg/constants and its correctness property is parity with that source, which a generator check should assert rather than mutation. techniques.ts and themes.ts stay excluded on a measurement, not a hunch: 96% of techniques.ts's 3144 mutants are static (module-level data), Stryker's own estimate for one shard was ~53 hours, and every one of the 13 mutants that did run returned Timeout, which the aggregate scores as caught. Admitting it whole would report thousands of clock-kills as assertion-kills. Their genuine logic (207 mutants across query, glossary and colour-derivation functions) is being split into separately mutated modules instead.
_comment_thresholds: high/low are display thresholds (the portal reads them for its ok/warn coloring); 'break' is deliberately absent. A break threshold here was a second, independent gate at 90 while the real floors live in api/mutation-floors.json (hooks 100, surface 97), which is the two-sources problem. The enforcing gate is each scope's aggregate job in nightly-mutation.yml, which reads its floor from that file, and every shard step already runs continue-on-error because the aggregate is the scope's gate. Do not reintroduce break without deleting the aggregate gates.
_comment_dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Instrumentation, not coverage analysis, is what makes the initial run slow: the suite is ~170s uninstrumented and exceeds 30 minutes with 6302 mutant switches inserted, measured both with perTest and with coverageAnalysis off, which timed out identically. Stryker's 5-minute default therefore aborts the whole run before a single mutant is tested. This is a ceiling, not a cost, and it sits well inside the job's 350-minute timeout. An initial run that needs more than this ceiling means the unsharded whole-surface run is infeasible and the work belongs in per-file shards, which is a finding worth failing on rather than absorbing into an ever-larger number.
_comment_ignorePatterns: Report artifact directories, none of which the tests read. Local allure-results alone holds ~422k files: unignored, ProjectReader spends ~100s walking them and the sandbox copy exhausts a tmpfs. A CI checkout is clean, so this matters for local iteration and costs CI nothing.
